note: Every source this archive has put a name to, whether or not it gave anything back. A search that returns nothing is a result: without it the next person repeats the work, and — worse — reads a silence as an absence. “Blocked” means a login wall, a bot check or an access denial this archive has chosen not to get round. “Not yet” means known, wanted, and not obtained. The register is kept by hand in sources/searched.json and validated by tools/searched.py.

read.book: Otočac municipal cemetery — 86 photographs, read out
read.pages: 84 usable frames, surveyed on contact sheets and the best read at full resolution
read.got: **Thirty-two legible memorials**, and the archive's Otočac surnames are all still in the churchyard: **Žubrinić** on at least eighteen stones, with **Orešković, Kostelac, Sekula, Prpić and Marić** among them. The oldest is a **Žubrinić family tomb** — an arch carved *ŽUBRINIĆ* over a wrought-iron cross, four ivy-covered plates: **Franjo ✽1846 †1925 · Ivanjica ✽1848 †1886 · Venceslav ✽1874 · Ju[v]ana**. The best-dated single stone is **Kata Kostelac, ✽10.3.1859 †2.6.1911**.
read.missed: **No stone names anyone already in this archive's tree.** The direct line at Otočac dies before the stones begin — ahnentafel 5 is buried at Senj, ahnentafel 10 and 20 have no death dates at all — and every dated memorial here is later. **A gravestone is a memorial, not a register**, carved by the living and wrong often enough to matter: the Senj stone in this archive gives Ljubomir's birth as 1891 where the register says 1892. **Nothing has been joined to the tree.**

read.book: Otočac baptisms 1846–1858 — the Conditio column, and a third Žubrinić house
read.pages: two openings, the Conditio column read cell by cell
read.got:
**A third Žubrinić house at Šumećica.** 21 December 1846: «**Thomas, filius Michaelis, legitimus** | ***Confiniar[ius] Šumećica 10*** | **Michael Žubrinić et ejus consors *Helena nata Orešković e Prozor*, Catholici**». **Not 2, not 24 — ten.**

And **the method is confirmed**: this book's *Conditio* gives **village and house for every entry**, not only for Žubrinići — the row above Thomas reads «*Confiniarius ex **Poljica 14***». So the column can be harvested.
read.missed: **The index's ARK points at the opening, not the row.** The 3 January 1855 entry the index calls *Mathias Žubrinić* is on a page whose sixth row is a **Marković** family; finding the right row costs two or three crops per entry, which is what makes this a sitting rather than a lookup. **Seven more indexed Michael entries remain unread.**

read.pages: one entry, read in three aligned chunks
read.got: «***Anno Domini 1857 die 1 Nbris. Ego Joannes Tušić, cooperator loci, baptizavi Josephum, filium legitimum, Romano-Catholicum, **Joannis Papa** et ejus uxoris **Mathiæ Pilipić**. Levantibus Patrinis … ✝ Michaël Stipančić.***» — **the baptism of ahnentafel 6**, to the day the tree gives, and his parents named. The godfather signs with a **cross**. And the surname: **the father is *Joannis Papa* here and *Juraj Papa* in his son's marriage of 1885 — never *Antić* in either.** The Senj register of 1857 is a prose book, not a ruled one.
read.missed: **The marriage of ahnentafel 12 and 13 is not in the index.** It must fall shortly before November 1857, in *Senj marriages 1734–1858*; the index reaches Senj baptisms of that year but not its marriages. That one is a film read.

read.pages: one entry, read in aligned chunks
read.got: **«1885, dne 3 Svibnja» — Josip Papić, *bremenar*, of Senj, aged 27**, son of ***«Juraj Papa, težak, i Matia rodjena Pilipić»***. **Ahnentafel 6's marriage, naming ahnentafel 12 and 13**, with an occupation for each: the son a **bremenar** — a carrier — the father a ***težak***. And the surname is written ***Papa***, not Antić, while the son is already ***Papić***: **the by-name hardening into a surname across one generation, in a single document.**
read.missed: The bride's own sub-row was **not** read cleanly. A *Franjo Perpić* stands in the next column but these pages are tilted and that column may be witnesses rather than the bride's parents — **ahnentafel 7's father is not being claimed from this.** The entry's second half, the witnesses and the officiant, are unread.

read.pages: one entry, read at full resolution in aligned chunks
read.got: «*Ego **Joës Antonius Ivankovich, Parochus Loci**, baptizavi Infantem **heri natum** ex **Georgio, et Maria Uroda, Conjugibus, hujus Loci**, cui impositum est Nomen **Joannis Georgij**. Patrini fuerunt **Ill[ustrissi]mus D[omi]nus Pro-Colonellus Joannes**…*» — **ahnentafel 54's parents, named**, and a **lieutenant-colonel** standing godfather. The tree's «born 22 April 1777» is the **baptism**: *heri natum* makes the birth **21 April**. With the index run, **seven children of Georgius and Maria Uroda, 1764–1784**.
read.missed: **Maria's maiden surname is not given** — she is simply *Maria Uroda, conjux*. Ahnentafel 109 is still a given name only. The godfather's territorial name, after «Pro-Colonellus Joannes», was not resolved and neither was the «Centurio Daniel» beside him.

read.book: Karlobag — Umrli 1774–1804 and its Kazalo, both opened for the first time
read.pages: the U column of the index, and folio 67 of the register
read.got: **A generation above ahnentafel 54, dated and buried.** The U column gives **six Urode in thirty years** — Heva (11 May, fol. 5), Joannes (6 July, fol. 23), **Georgius (10 September, fol. 67)**, Petrus (7 Nov., fol. 82), Jacobus (22 July, fol. 85). Folio 67 is image 390's right-hand page, headed *Anno Domini 1791*, and under *Septembris* it reads: «***Dñus Georgius Uroda**, munitus omnibus Sacramentis, [in domo] sua obiit, atque die **12ᵃ** sepultus est **in propria [sua Crypta ante] fores Ecclesiæ Parochialis** existente*.» **Died 10 September 1791, buried in his own crypt before the church door.**

A family that buries in its own crypt in 1791 producing a fisherman by 1846 is a descent that needs a document. **Karlobag births 1771–1804, DGS 5481648, with its own Kazalo, would give it in one entry.**

read.book: Rijeka marriages 1866–1891 — the last five months of the book
read.pages: seventeen openings, every entry's names read
read.got: **The book ends on 9 August 1891.** Image 716 is the END OF FILM target and image 715 is a ruled blank struck through with a diagonal. Every marriage from **April to 9 August 1891** is now read — roughly 120 entries, entry numbers 115 to 207 — and the names are a portrait of Rijeka rather than of Lika: **Cesare · Demarchi · Marchesi · Buzzoduro · Colella · Magarelli · Duggeri Rolla · Casarni · Bellini · Capudi** beside **Kljun · Zadnik · Vrsalović · Mihalčić · Matejčić · Zorčić · Žurić · Šusterić · Marušić · Žukavić**.

read.book: Otočac baptisms 1834–1846 — where the house number is and is not written
read.pages: two openings, chosen from the record index
read.got: **The record index hands out the image ARK of every entry**, so an indexed baptism opens at the page directly instead of being hunted down a film. That gives **276 Otočac Žubrinić index entries for 1834–1862 — about 138 baptisms**, each one openable. **Michael has twenty-three to at least eight different mothers; Nicolaus has exactly two**, and those two are the pair read at the page this morning, both at Šumećica N° 2.
read.missed: **The 1834–1846 book does not record house numbers.** Its *Conditio* cell holds one status word — *Confiniarius*, *Decurio*, *Limitaneus* — with no village and no number, checked at **December 1839** and **March 1845**; the place column gives only «Ottoccii», the place of baptism. Ahnentafel 10's own January 1834 entry, «*ex pago Shumechicza N° 24*», is an early-book habit the parish dropped. **So the house numbers are readable for 1846–1858 and for the first years of the 1834 book, and not in between** — which narrows the plan that was written this morning.

read.book: Otočac — Status animarum 1710–1846, the Šumećica block
read.pages: 22 openings surveyed for the village margin; images 102, 103 read household by household
read.got: **The book is navigable.** The *Pagus* margin was called unreadable by the last sitting; it was rotated the wrong way. The village is written **bottom-to-top** in the gutter — rotate **+90°**, not −90°, and it reads at a glance. That produced the village map of the whole census, and it puts **Šumećica at images 102–106 — five openings, the whole village**, between *Beljue* and a second run of *Luka*, with an ***Extinctæ*** section at 108–109. Read at the page: **Domus 9, Josephus Dašović** (nine members, with *Anna uxor Petri nata Žunić*) and **Domus 4, Mattheus Orehović** (fourteen, with *Martha uxor Georgii nata Orehović*). The **N° Domus column is at x≈0.19–0.23**, not 0.16, and the numbers are **not in order** — 9 then 4 — so the book cannot be walked to a house number.
read.missed: **Domus 2 and Domus 24 were not reached, and no Žubrinić household has appeared at Šumećica yet.** Images 104, 105 and 106 are unread, so this is not a finding — but it is odd, because the census carries births to 1846 and ahnentafel 20 is at «ex pago Shumechicza N° 24» in January 1834. Either he is on those three openings, or the family sits in the *Extinctæ* section. FamilySearch then refused the session — 403 on an ark that had worked minutes earlier, still 403 after forty seconds, which is the block and not the blip.

rows.src: Otočac cemetery — photographed on the ground, October 2024
rows.what: Whether the churchyard names anyone this archive already holds
rows.got:
**Eighty-six photographs, thirty-two legible memorials, and one real connection — to Arcanum rather than to the tree.**

**The find is a Žubrinić family tomb**: an arch carved ***ŽUBRINIĆ*** above a wrought-iron cross, with four ivy-covered name-plates —

> **FRANJO ✽1846. †1925.** · **IVANJICA ✽1848. †1886.** · **VENCESLAV ✽1874. †19…** · **JU[V]ANA ✽18… †193…**

**«Venceslav» is why this matters.** The Arcanum harvest of yesterday found, in the *Mihók-féle Magyar Compass* of **1908**, the board of the **Srpska štedionica dioničarsko društvo u Otočcu** — the Serbian savings bank — with **«Kassier Venzeslav Žubrinić»** as its cashier. **A Venceslav Žubrinić born 1874 would be thirty-four in 1908.** Same rare given name, same town, right age. **The printed record and the stone are very likely the same man**, and this archive now has his dates and his grave.

**Every Otočac surname the archive married into is still in that churchyard** — **Orešković** (Katica ✽25.V.1882 †29.XI.1932, on a crowned-Virgin monument), **Kostelac** (Kata ✽10.3.1859 †2.6.1911, the best-dated stone there), **Sekula**, **Prpić**, **Marić**.

**And one stone argues this archive's own thesis in carved letters:** *«OBITELJI **ŽUBRINIĆ-ČUN** i ŽANIĆ»*, Josip ✽1894 †1957 and Julka ✽1892 †1980. **A nadimak, hyphenated onto the surname on a twentieth-century headstone** — the practice the registers show in the 1800s, still doing its work.
rows.missed:
**No stone names anyone already in the tree, and that is the honest headline.** The direct line at Otočac dies before these memorials begin: ahnentafel 5 is buried at **Senj**, and ahnentafel 10, 20, 40 and 42 have no death date at all. Every dated stone here is later than the people this archive can name.

**Nothing has been joined.** A gravestone is a memorial, not a register — carved by the living, often long afterwards, and wrong often enough to matter: the Senj stone in this archive gives Ljubomir's birth as **1891** where the register says **1892**. The Venceslav identification is an argument from a name, a town and an age, and it is labelled as one.

rows.src: The archive's own data — fifteen drawers published as parents
rows.what: Why every Žubrinić page showed a single-letter relative
rows.got:
**A reader asked what the single-letter Žubrinići were, and whether the site was saying they were related. It was.**

Fifteen nodes are named with one capital letter and a surname — **A · B · C · F · G · H · J · L · M · N · P · R · S · T · W**, every one *«X Žubrinić Xubrinich Zubrinic»*, with **no birth, no death, no place and no source**. **Each is entered as the parent of every Žubrinić whose name begins with that letter** — *M* fathers Mathæus, Michael and Mate; *T* three men called Thomas — **and they are entered as one another's siblings**. So the tree asserted **fifteen brothers and sisters called A through W**, hanging from nothing, with **75 real people** beneath them across **285 relationship links**.

**The giveaway is the sorting.** *Jure / Georgius / Juraj* is filed under **G**, not J — the letter follows the Latin form, not the displayed name. That is a card index, not a household. One drawer breaks even its own rule: **Nicolai Žubrinić is filed under M**.

**Why the existing detector missed them.** `/buckets` looks for the words a researcher writes when they know they are guessing — *sorting*, *working*, *unknown*, *brothers of*. **A drawer labelled «M» contains none of them.**

**Fixed in the data layer, so every page benefits.** Both the bucket detector and the site's own junk filter now test for it — one capital letter, a surname, and **no date of any kind**, strict on purpose so a real person recorded by an initial is not swept up. **Buckets 21 → 36; people standing on one, 218 → 293; pages 2,232 → 2,202.** And the gap is now **stated rather than blank**: the **142** people whose only parent was a drawer get a notice naming the label instead of an empty space.

**The GEDCOM is untouched.** This changes what the archive publishes, not the tree — the separation the project rests on.

rows.src: FamilySearch — Šumećica by house number, from the Otočac Conditio column
rows.what: The fifteen indexed Michael Žubrinić baptisms of 1846–58, by house number
rows.got:
**Six houses, four villages, and question 4d answered.** The 1846–58 Otočac baptism book writes the household into its *Conditio* column, and the record index gives the image ARK of every indexed entry, so each opens at the page. Fifteen indexed Žubrinić baptisms in that window have a father whose name is a Michael variant — *Michael · Michaël · Miho · Mio · Miha · Miko*. **Fourteen are read.**

The households are **Šumećica N° 5** (four children, 1849–58), **Šumećica N° 10**, **Poljica N° 13**, **Prozor N° 50**, **Obilje N° 7** and **Prozor Br. 1**, with **six distinct wives**. **The twenty-three Michael baptisms are not one man**, and the Conditio column is the only thing that separates them.

**Šumećica N° 5 is new** — Michael Žubrinić and Maria Marković, four children between 1849 and 1858. The Šumećica houses known before were N° 2, N° 10 and N° 24.

**Three Žubrinić women married Žubrinić men** — Catharina at Obilje N° 7, Kata at Prozor Br. 1, and a third on the same page as the 1858 entry — and **the index gives a given name only for every one of them.** The index is also wrong at least once: it records the 1852 mother at Šumećica N° 5 as «Maria Maković» where the register says **Marković**, making one household look like two.

**Three cautions are recorded** for whoever reads the rest of this book. It **changes language from page to page** — one January 1852 opening is Croatian on the left and Latin on the right, so *Confiniarius … N°* becomes *Graničar iz … Br.* The **status word drifts while the house number holds**: the Šumećica N° 5 father is *Graničar*, *Gregarius*, *Confiniarius* and *Rusticus* in turn, and reading the trade as an identity would split one family into four. And the **numbering practice begins inside the book** — July and August 1846 are bare.

**One entry outstanding**, Maria of 28 November 1858, stopped by the block and not by the book.

**Reconciled against the tree.** These are not new people — all six wives and nine of the fourteen children are already in it. **What the tree lacked was the house number**: of those nine children exactly one carried one, *Nikola Miko Žubrinić* at «Prozor 50», which this reading independently confirms, while the rest give «Otočac, Croatia» or nothing. Seven readings are recorded against their people, and **five children the tree does not have** are recorded beside it — each with siblings the tree already holds, so they are gaps inside known families rather than an unknown branch.
rows.missed: **The index's ARK points at the opening, not the row**, so each entry costs two or three crops to locate; the page the index calls *Mathias Žubrinić, 3 January 1855* has a **Marković** family in its sixth row. **Seven indexed Michael Žubrinić entries between 1847 and 1858 are still unread**, and with them the rest of the house map.

rows.src: FamilySearch — Tonka Blažević's baptism, and an index that is wrong
rows.what: 25 October 1884 by this archive's reading against 27 November 1884 by the index
rows.got:
**The register settles it, and the register says this archive was right.**

Krmpote, entry **66** of 1884, read at full resolution: «***Godine 1884 dne 25. 27. Listopada*** — **Tonka** — *zakonita* — **Tome Blažević i Tereza rodjena Pećanić, rim. kat. seljani** — **Smokvica kbroj 114**».

***Listopada* is October.** So **Tonka was born 25 October 1884 and baptised on the 27th** — the archive's earlier date was the **birth**, and correct.

**The FamilySearch index's «27 November 1884» is wrong.** It has the day right and the month wrong — *Listopada* (October) read as *Studenoga* (November). **An index is a finding aid and not a record**, and this is the cleanest demonstration of it this archive has: the index found the entry, and then misdated it by a month.

**It also makes a third document for Smokvica kbroj 114**, and a fourth appearance of **Tereza *rodjena* Pećanić** alive and bearing children in 1884 — which the tree's old «died before 1850» could never have allowed.
rows.missed: **The letter to Župa Krmpote, sent this morning, asks the parish this very question.** It cannot be unsent. If an answer comes it will confirm what is written here — and a nil return still tells us whether the parish holds the original. **Recorded so that the reply is read against this and not the other way round.**

rows.src: FamilySearch record index — ahnentafel 6's baptism, ahnentafel 7's parents, a new Antić child
rows.what: Items 1, 2 and 3 of the standing list
rows.got:
**Three answers in one sitting, and one of them corrects me.**

**1 · Ahnentafel 6's baptism, read at the page.** Senj, «*Anno Domini 1857 die 1 Nbris. Ego **Joannes Tušić**, cooperator loci, baptizavi **Josephum**, filium legitimum, Romano-Catholicum, **Joannis Papa** et ejus uxoris **Mathiæ Pilipić**. Levantibus Patrinis … ✝ **Michaël Stipančić***.» The date matches the tree exactly, the parents are named, and the godfather signs with a **cross**.

**The surname is the finding.** The father is entered ***Joannis Papa*** in 1857 and ***Juraj Papa*** in 1885 — **and never *Antić* in either**. The *nadimak* has displaced the surname outright in the Senj register by 1857, and hardens into *Papić* for the son. Two documents, twenty-eight years apart, and the change is visible between them.

**2 · Ahnentafel 7's father — and I was right to doubt myself.** Yesterday a *Franjo Perpić* stood in the column beside the 1885 marriage and I refused to claim it because the page is tilted. **The index's own role list settles it:** *Father-in-law **Ivan Perpić**, Mother-in-law **Luce Perpić***. **Ahnentafel 14 is Ivan**, as the tree has it, and Franjo was a witness. Ahnentafel 15 is confirmed as **Luce** — her maiden surname still unrecorded.

**3 · A child of ahnentafel 24 and 25 that this archive does not have.** «**Maria Rosaria Antić, 4 October 1847**, Selce — Father **Josephus Antić**, Mother **Maria Jellićić**». Checked against the tree: **she is not in it.** A younger sister for ahnentafel 12.
rows.missed: **Selce deaths are not indexed** — the index reaches that parish's *baptisms*, roughly 1826–1889, and the roles are always principal-plus-parents. The six direct-line deaths at Selce (ahnentafel 24, 25, 48, 49, 50, 51) still need the film, **DGS 5497948**. **And the marriage of ahnentafel 12 and 13 is not indexed either** — it falls just before November 1857, in *Senj marriages 1734–1858*.

rows.src: FamilySearch — the session signed out, and seven items stopped with it
rows.what: Bribir · Sv. Juraj kod Senja · Senj marriages · Selce deaths · the Karlobag census · the Grižane Popis duša · the unread Otočac village
rows.got:
**A third failure state, and it is not either of the two this archive had already written down.**

    fetch('/service/search/hr/v2/personas?…')  →  503
    location.hostname                          →  «ident.familysearch.org»
    document.title                             →  «Sign-in to your account»

**Every request — API and page alike — redirects to the sign-in host.** Not a 403 on the tile service: a **503 and a redirect**, with the browser sitting on the login page.

**How to tell it from the other two.** A rate-limit blip and a session block both leave you **logged in** — the catalogue, the record index and the ordinary site keep answering, and only the deep-zoom tiles refuse. **A sign-out takes everything.**

**It cannot be waited out and must not be worked around.** The only fix is for the account holder to sign in again in this browser. **No credentials were typed and none will be** — not the user's, not from a password store. The right move is to say the session expired, name what it blocks, and stop.

**What carried on regardless:** Arcanum, which needs no FamilySearch session, and the local data work. The sitting lost seven items and kept the rest.

**And it arrived after a long run of catalogue and record-index queries, not after heavy tile fetching** — so it reads as ordinary session expiry rather than anything provoked. Written into `tools/familysearch.md` beside the blip-versus-block test.

rows.src: Arcanum — the Smojvers of Karlobag in the Hungarian state record
rows.what: The four Smojvers in the 1884 officials' directory, followed up
rows.got:
**A family's public life across thirty-three years, in the town whose parish registers this archive has been reading.** *Smojver* is **ahnentafel 53 and 106**.

**A registered company, and a woman who signed for it.** The ***Központi Értesítő*** — the **official gazette of the Hungarian company register** — carries the firm three times. **30 July 1905**: «*Odpremnički posao **Dragutina Smojvera** … **Smojver Károly szállító üzlete**. Főtelep **Karlobag**. A czég tulajdonosa Smojver Károly, ki feleségét **Smojver Ljubicát** …*». Then **8 September 1907** and **14 May 1908** record that **Ljubica Smojver's *czégjegyzési jogosultság* — her legal right to sign for the firm — was registered and then struck off.** **A woman holding power of attorney over a Croatian coastal haulage company in 1905**, gazetted in Budapest.

**The same man at school, twenty-two years earlier.** *Horvát gimnázium, Fiume, 1883*, p. 134: «*… 35 **Smojver Dragutin — Selce** …*» — with a **Prpić of Karlobag** two lines above him. Selce is this archive's own place.

**Three Smojvers in the revenue service** — **Iván**, *tiszt* of the Finance Ministry (1890); **János**, *pénztárnok* at Belovár (1906–07); and **József**, ***ellenőr***, controller — in 1908 **at the Karlobag sub-customs office itself**.

**And two wounded.** *Veszteség lajstrom*, 27 March 1915: «**Karlobag 1882 verw Smojver Mijo, ResZugsf, IR Nr 79**» and «**Korenica 1892 verw Smojver Blaž, ResKorp**», same regiment, same list. This archive already holds six Žubrinići in these lists.

**Nothing here is joined to the tree**, and that is stated plainly — not one of these people has been matched to a baptism. The seam gives **the shape of a surname's public life** in exactly the town and decades where the registers have the family. Page images are paywalled; all of it is the free snippet, quoted as returned.

rows.src: FamilySearch record index — an index-first sweep of the unread direct line
rows.what: Which of the twelve unread direct-line ancestors the index can reach
rows.got:
**Twelve people on the direct line had no reading. The index was run at all of them in one sitting, and it found two.**

**Ahnentafel 6 and 7 — married at Senj, 3 May 1885.** «*Josip Papić, **bremenar**, of Senj, aged 27*», son of «***Juraj Papa, težak, i Matia rodjena Pilipić***». That is **ahnentafel 12 and 13 named in a register**, each with a trade, and it catches the surname mid-change: **the father is entered as *Papa*, the son as *Papić***. The archive has argued for years that *Papa* is a **nadimak** attached to *Antić*; here it is being used as the surname outright, and hardening into *Papić* in the next generation. *(The tree gives ahnentafel 6 a birth of 1 November 1857; aged 27 in May 1885 agrees.)*

**Ahnentafel 53 — a lead, not a finding.** «*Smoj[v]er, 23 February 1782, Karlobag — father **Vincentio**, mother **Oliva***». Ahnentafel 53 is **Oliva Maria Smojver, born March 1781**, and a Karlobag Smojver household with a mother called **Oliva** the following year is the right shape. **Her own baptism is not indexed** — the index reaches only about four Karlobag Smojver entries before 1796 against 114 after — so this is a page to open, not a join to make.

**And the negatives are worth as much.** **Ahnentafel 20, 21, 32, 40, 41, 52** are all before their parishes' filmed registers begin, or fall in the unindexed early years: Otočac births start **1834**, Krmpote **1879**. **Ahnentafel 15, 16 and 22 have no dates at all**, so there is nothing to search on. **Those six are not reachable by index and never will be** — they need the page or a parish office.

rows.src: FamilySearch record index — Krmpote-Vodice, the children of ahnentafel 8 and 9
rows.what: Juraj Blažević's baptism, and whether Ledenice or Novi Vinodolski holds it
rows.got:
**Krmpote-Vodice is in the record index**, under the place string *«Krmpote-Vodice, Modrus-Fiume, Mađarska»*, and the index hands out **the image ARK of every entry**. Filtering 22,000 Blaževići down to the Vinodol parishes gives **ahnentafel 8 and 9 as a couple in the register**:

| | child | |
|---|---|---|
| **1880** | **Marija** | `3:1:3QS7-L99X-PLTH` |
| **25 Aug 1882** | **Ivan** | `3:1:3QS7-899X-PL39` |
| **27 Nov 1884** | **Tonka** | `3:1:3QS7-899X-PLHV` |

**Three children to *Tome Blažević i Terezija Pećanić*, and none after 1884.** Marija and Ivan are precisely the two siblings question 1f leans on — *«Ive Blažević sin Tomin»* and *«Marija Blažević ćer Tomina»*, godparents at Marijan's baptism in 1895. **They were tree-facts; they are now register entries**, openable at the page in one step.

Ivan's read out: «**zakonit** · **Toma Blažević i Tereza njegova rodjena Pećanić — rim. kat. seljaci** · **Smokvica kbroj 114** · kumovi **Pere Pećanić i Marija Butorac supruga Jandrina**». Born the 25th, baptised the 26th.
rows.missed:
**Juraj's own baptism is not there, and now definitively.** The Krmpote book begins in **1879** and he was fathering children from 1892; the index shows **no Juraj to Toma and Terezija** in it. **Ledenice and Novi Vinodolski were checked the same way and hold no candidate either.** His baptism is not in this collection — which leaves the parish office, and the letter already drafted for it.

**A method caution, learnt twice today.** These pages are tilted, and a wide crop across a row lands on *different entries* at its two ends — the house number **138** sitting in the crop first looked like this family's and belongs to the entry above. Crop one row, confirm its left and right edges belong together, then read.

rows.src: FamilySearch record index — the Karlobag Urode, and a generation added
rows.what: Ahnentafel 54's baptism, his parents, and who married in 1806
rows.got:
**A generation added to the direct line, and the family it adds is not the family this archive thought it had.**

**The route is the reusable part.** The Karlobag births are in the record index, and the index payload carries **the image ARK of every entry** — so no film had to be hunted. 257 Urode in the collection; filtering in hand on **Karlobag** leaves **41**; sorting by date produces a family at once:

**Georgius Uroda and Maria** — *Dominicus* 1764 · *Petrus Jacobus* 1767 · *Heva Joanna* 1769 · *Maria Catharina* 1772 · **_Joannis Georgÿ_ 22 April 1777** · *Anton Joanis* 1780 · *Joannis* 1784. **Seven children over twenty years**, and the two eldest names close a loop with the 1774–1804 death index read the same day, which buries a **Uroda Heva** and a **Uroda Petrus**.

**Read at the page**, folio 36/37, *Anno Dñi 1777*, under *Aprilis*:

> «*Ego **Joës Antonius Ivankovich, Parochus Loci**, baptizavi Infantem **heri natum** ex **Georgio, et Maria Uroda, Conjugibus, hujus Loci**, cui impositum est Nomen **Joannis Georgij**. Patrini fuerunt **Ill[ustrissi]mus D[omi]nus Pro-Colonellus Joannes**…*»

**Three things in one sentence.** The tree's «born 22 April 1777» is the **baptism** — *heri natum* puts the birth on the **21st**. **Ahnentafel 108 and 109 are named.** And **the godfather is a lieutenant-colonel** — nobody asks a *Pro-Colonellus* to stand for a fisherman's son.

**It corroborates the crypt.** *Dominus* Georgius Uroda, dead 10 September 1791 and buried in his own crypt at the church door, fathers children from 1764 to 1784 without strain. **The Urode were not fishermen in the 1770s.** They are that by 1834 and 1846. A family coming down in the world across two generations, now visible in documents instead of inferred.

**And yesterday's doubt is answered from a page already read.** The 1806 marriage of *«Joannis filii defuncti Dñi Georgij Uroda»* to **Maria filia Nicolai Barletich** raised the question whether ahnentafel 55 was a Barletich rather than the tree's «Gerkacs». **She is not.** Ahnentafel 27's baptism of 23 April 1810 — read earlier this month — gives the godmother as **«Maria conjux Joannis Uroda»**. Two different couples: **Georgius** with his Maria fathering ahnentafel 27, and **Joannes** with *his* Maria standing godmother to her. **Brother and brother** — so the 1806 groom is the **1784** child and **the tree's Maria Gerkacs survives.**

rows.src: FamilySearch — Karlobag, the death index of 1774–1804
rows.what: The Georgius Uroda whom the 1806 marriage calls «defunctus»
rows.got:
**Found, and he is not what this archive expected the Urode to be.**

The death index this archive already knows — fourteen Urode, 1805–1846 — belongs to the *later* book, and its earliest Uroda is 1808. A man dead before February 1806 had to be in the **Umrli 1774–1804**, and **that book has its own alphabetical Kazalo at images 410–434** which nobody here had opened. Its letters run one page-group each: **T·U at image 431**.

**Six Urode in thirty years** — Heva, Joannes, **Georgius**, Petrus, Jacobus — none of them known here. Georgius is entered **10 7bris, folio 67**.

The left-hand pages carry the even folios — 62 at image 388, 64 at 389, 66 at 390 — so **folio 67 is image 390's right-hand page**, headed ***Anno Domini 1791***. Under *Septembris*:

> «***Dñus Georgius Uroda**, munitus omnibus Sacramentis, [in domo] sua obiit, atque die **12ᵃ** sepultus est **in propria [sua Crypta ante] fores Ecclesiæ Parochialis** existente.*»

**Died 10 September 1791; buried on the 12th in his own crypt before the doors of the parish church.**

**This changes the Urode.** The archive has carried them as **fishermen** — ahnentafel 55 buried in 1834 as *«uxor **piscatoris** Georgii Uroda»*, ahnentafel 54 in 1846 as *«annorum 72, **piscator**»*. **The man of 1791 is a *Dominus*, dies fortified with all the sacraments in his own house, and is buried in a crypt his family owns at the church door** — and the 1806 marriage still calls him *Dñi Georgij Uroda* fifteen years later, with the **village judge** witnessing his son's wedding.

**Not claimed: that ahnentafel 54 descends from him.** Born about 1774, he would have been seventeen in 1791 and could be a second son — but a crypt-owning family producing a fisherman by 1846 is a descent that needs a document, not an inference. **Karlobag births 1771–1804 (DGS 5481648, with its own index) would give it in one entry.**

rows.src: FamilySearch — Rijeka marriages, April to the end of the book
rows.what: Juraj Blažević × Tereza Žubrinić, the marriage question 1b asks for
rows.got:
**Seventeen openings read, and the book turns out to stop earlier than its label.**

The catalogue calls it *Vjenčani 1866–1891*. **The last entry is 9 August 1891** — image 716 is the END OF FILM target and 715 is a ruled blank struck through. Every marriage from **April to 9 August 1891** has now been read at the page, entry numbers **115 to 207**, and **there is no Blažević and no Žubrinić among them.**

The names are the finding in their own way. This is a **port city register, not a Lika one** — *Cesare, Demarchi, Marchesi, Buzzoduro, Colella, Magarelli, Duggeri Rolla, Bellini, Capudi* beside *Kljun, Zadnik, Vrsalović, Mihalčić, Matejčić, Zorčić, Žurić, Marušić*. Two surnames of this archive's own appear and are **not** ours: **Michaël Papić × Agnes Brunović**, and **Josephus Prpić × Marica Zinić**, both June–July 1891.

**And the structural point matters more than the negative.** Ljubomir was born at Rijeka on **1 March 1892**. A marriage between **9 August 1891** and that birth **would not be on this film at all** — it falls into exactly the same filming gap that swallows his baptism, where the births jump 1891 → 1900. **Two documents, one hole.**

**What is not claimed:** the couple could have married at Rijeka in 1889, 1890 or early 1891. That is images 1–698 of this film and was not opened.

rows.src: FamilySearch — Karlobag marriages, folios 2 to 6 read out
rows.what: Ahnentafel 54's marriage — and what was there instead
rows.got:
**Five folios, seven years, every groom named — and a generation nobody had.**

The window a daughter born **23 April 1810** allows is 1804–1810, and it is now read at the page: **folio 2** (1804–06) Potocniak · Luksetich · Luccich · Sepst · Allagetich · Millatich · **folio 3** (1806) **Uroda** · Mandekich · Kiricich · Smoyver · **folio 4** (1807) Locatelli · Dovcich · Hudak · Gergas · Kriskovich · **folio 5** (1807–09) Korpić · Medvidich · Kriskovich · Sesich · Kosner · Dorstiacich · Lenach · Sikka · **folio 6** (1809–10) Miletich · Sirola · Vukelich · Kovačević.

**No Uroda × Gerkacs anywhere in them.** What is there is one Uroda entry, 10 February 1806:

> «…habito mutuo consensu ***Joannis filii defuncti Dñi Georgij Uroda*** ac ***Mariæ filiæ Nicolai Barletich***, hujatium… conjunxi ego Joës **Antonius Frankovich Parochus loci**, præsentibus Georgio Jerko et **Gregorio Matthossich Judice Loci**.»

**A Georgius Uroda dead before February 1806, styled *Dominus*, with a son Joannes marrying before the village judge.** Nothing in this archive has ever stood above ahnentafel 54.

**It is not his marriage.** Ahnentafel 55's death of 1834 reads «uxor piscatoris ***Georgii*** Uroda» — her husband was a Georgius, dead 1846 at 72. This groom is a **Joannes**. The likeliest shape is **two brothers, Joannes and Georgius, sons of the dead Georgius senior** — and that puts a question to the tree, which carries ahnentafel 54 as ***«Joannis Georgius Uroda»***, exactly what a tree program produces when it flattens ***Joannes filius Georgii***. **Nothing has been added to the tree.**

**Method, learned the hard way:** the page is **tilted**, so cropping a wide entry as a left half and a right half lands on **different lines**. Read in three chunks with the same y-range and overlapping x, or the sentence assembles itself wrongly — as it did here, first making Georgius the groom.

rows.src: FamilySearch record index — Otočac, 1853, tested for density
rows.what: Lucca Žubrinić, born 1853, the tree's sister for Tereza
rows.got:
**The tree's Lucca is not in the register, and this time the negative can be trusted.**

When this was first noticed the objection was obvious: *the index may simply not cover 1853*. **It does.** Otočac Žubrinić entries by year —

| 1851 | 1852 | **1853** | 1854 | 1855 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15 | 8 | **13** | 9 | 11 |

**1853 sits in the middle of its neighbours.** It is not a gap.

And in that year there is **no Lucca and no Luce Žubrinić baptised at Otočac**, and **no child at all to a father called Nicolaus**. The only Lucia of 1853 is **Lucia *Kostelac***, daughter of Stephanus Kostelac and Barbara Žubrinić — a Žubrinić mother, not a Žubrinić child. The Žubrinić Lucias either side are **Luce, 30 June 1850**, to *Mio Žubrinić and Jele Orešković*, and **Lucia, 16 March 1855**, to *Jacobus Žubrinić and Martha*.

**So the entry that would make ahnentafel 10 a father at nineteen has no register behind it.** The tree gives Tereza a sister Lucca born 1853 and dead in 1871; the parish that would have baptised her, in a year the index covers normally, did not.

**Stated carefully:** an index is a finding aid, not a register, and a single missed page is always possible. But the density test is the thing that was missing in the morning, and it has now been run.

rows.src: FamilySearch record index — the Otočac Žubrinić baptisms, and the ARK trick
rows.what: Rebuilding the Šumećica Žubrinić households by house number
rows.got:
**The index gives the image, and that is worth more than any single reading.** The search service is `/service/search/hr/v2/personas`, and each entry's payload carries **the image ARK** beside the child, the date and both parents — so an indexed baptism can be opened at the page without hunting a film for it. **No earlier sitting used this.**

Two cautions found the hard way: **`q.birthLikePlace` does not bind** — the place has to be filtered in hand on the string **«Otočac, Küstenland, Austria»** — and **every baptism is indexed twice**, once per parent role, so a raw count doubles.

**276 Otočac Žubrinić entries, 1834–1862 — about 138 baptisms.** Normalising the index's own spelling scatter (*Zubrinić · Žubrinić · Xubrinić · Žubrinich · Zabrinić · Dubrinić · **Bubrinić***), the fathers run **Joannes ~22 · Michael ~23 · Matthaeus 7 · Franciscus 6 · Georgius 5 · Thomas 5 · Nicolaus 2**.

**Michael's twenty-three are to at least eight different mothers** — Maria, Catharina, Magdalena, Helena, Maria Marković, Maria Rogić, Magdalena Draženović, Anna Bobinac, Maria Maković, Helena Orešković. **That is not one man; it is a village full of Michaels**, which is precisely the trap question 4d is about.

**And a correction to this morning's plan.** The redirection assumed every baptism writes «e Šumećica N° X» into the *Conditio* column. **The 1834–1846 book does not** — its *Conditio* holds a single status word, checked at December 1839 and March 1845. The 1846–1858 book does. **The house numbers are readable for 1846–1858 and the first years of 1834, and not in between.**

rows.src: FamilySearch catalogue — every parish this family touches, film by film
rows.what: Juraj Blažević's baptism at Krmpote — and, when that failed, what FamilySearch actually holds
rows.got:
**Juraj's baptism is not reachable, and the reason rewrote the holdings table.**

Two sittings took parish ranges from the collection **waypoints**. The **catalogue item** goes a level deeper and lists the contents of every film, volume by volume, with the **DGS number** that reopens it. The query term is **`q.keywords`** — `q.text`, `q.anyPlace` and `q.placeString` are all rejected by that service, which is very likely why no earlier sitting used it. Six calls produced **`sources/familysearch/holdings.psv`: 79 films, named.**

**Four parishes were missing from the table entirely** — **Bribir** (its own parish, previously filed here as a *village of Grižane*, with registers back to **1678**), **Sv. Juraj kod Senja** (1695–1868), **Jurjevo**, and **Trsat**.

**And Rijeka, carried as «unknown — NOT CHECKED», is filmed 1590–1920** with alphabetical *Kazalo* indexes.

rows.src: FamilySearch — Rijeka, and the answer to question 13
rows.what: Ljubomir Blažević's baptism, Rijeka, 1892 — and Juraj's marriage to Tereza before it
rows.got:
**Question 13 has an answer and it is a negative.**

Rijeka's baptisms are filmed almost continuously from **1594**. The volumes run

· *Rođeni 1880–1886* · *1886–1890* · **_1890–1891_** · **_1900–1901_**

**There is no 1892–1899 birth register on the film**, and the birth *Kazalo* runs 1800–1889 and then 1895–1902. **Ljubomir's 1892 baptism cannot be reached on FamilySearch by image or by index.** It has to come from the Rijeka state archive or the parish — which is exactly what the drafted, unsent letter asks for. **That letter is now the only route.**

**One target is reachable.** *Vjenčani 1866–1891*, **DGS 5497940, 720 images**, covers «Juraj's marriage to Tereza before 1892» — the document question 1b asks for. Fixed point read at the page: **image 701 = May 1891, entries 115–121**; image 720 ends the book. **Images 699, 700 and 701 were read name by name** — Cesare, Kljun, Zadnik, Martić, Leopar, Švić, Vrsalović, Mihalčić, Terzaga, Matejčić, Sirola, Larber, Demarchi, Peharović. Rijeka town names. **No Blažević and no Žubrinić in April–May 1891.**

**Images 702–720 — June to December 1891 — are the remaining window**, and expectation should be a negative: a Lika man and an Otočac woman would marry in her parish or his, and **Otočac marriages stop in 1872 while Krmpote has no marriage book at all**. If Rijeka does not hold them, the marriage is not on FamilySearch anywhere — and that turns question 1b into a letter.
